title: Check if a number is prime
description: Write a function `is_prime(n)` that returns whether `n` is a prime number (an integer greater than 1 with no divisors other than 1 and itself).
hints: Idea to consider: check every possible divisor from 2 up to n itself
If n has any divisor d (2 <= d < n) where n % d == 0, it isn't prime - a single loop checking each candidate divisor answers the question.
Return False immediately if n < 2. Otherwise loop d from 2 to n - 1, returning False the moment n % d == 0 is found; if the loop finishes without finding one, return True.
expected_behavior: Returns True if n is prime, False otherwise.
explanation: Returning False as soon as a divisor is found avoids checking the rest of the range unnecessarily - the loop only needs one counterexample to disprove primality, but has to check every candidate to confirm it.
